research_mode: official MHCLG, Home Office and GOV.UK guidance only; building evacuation plan, enforcement, toolkit and competent-assessor methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Building emergency evacuation plan duty
verified_claims: The responsible person for an in-scope building must prepare a building emergency evacuation plan, share it with the local Fire and Rescue Authority and place a copy in the secure information box where one exists.
limitations: Plan preparation does not establish operational suitability or resident awareness.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Building-plan review and redistribution
verified_claims: The building emergency evacuation plan must be reviewed within 12 months, annually thereafter and when updating is needed; amended plans must be reshared and replaced in the secure box where applicable.
limitations: A review record does not prove that the Fire and Rescue Authority received the current version.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Resident instructions in building plan
verified_claims: The building emergency evacuation plan must include a copy of the resident instructions required by the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022.
limitations: Including instructions does not prove they were separately distributed or understood.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Relevant-resident status in building plan
verified_claims: The building emergency evacuation plan must state whether relevant residents are present.
limitations: The plan should not expose unnecessary personal data or replace the prescribed resident-information record.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Other evacuation arrangements in building plan
verified_claims: The plan must include information about other building evacuation arrangements, such as an evacuation alert system where relevant.
limitations: Listing an arrangement does not establish commissioning, maintenance or suitability.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Building-plan and fire-risk-assessment alignment
verified_claims: The building emergency evacuation plan must align with the property's fire-risk assessment.
limitations: Document consistency does not prove the underlying fire-risk assessment is suitable and sufficient.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Broader Residential PEEPs measures
verified_claims: The building plan should include broader measures arising from Residential PEEPs that benefit multiple residents, such as handrails or signage.
limitations: A measure's inclusion does not prove installation, inspection or effectiveness.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Evacuation-lift protocol in building plan
verified_claims: Where a building has an evacuation lift, the plan should explain how it is intended to be used during a fire.
limitations: An intended-use statement does not prove lift availability, protected operation or trained staffing.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Combining evacuation and building plans
verified_claims: The building emergency evacuation plan may be combined with floor plans or the building plan required by the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022.
limitations: Combining documents must not obscure required information or version control.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Residential PEEPs enforcing authority
verified_claims: Fire Safety Order enforcing authorities, including Fire and Rescue Authorities, can inspect and enforce responsible-person compliance with Residential PEEPs duties.
limitations: Enforcement powers do not mean a particular building has been inspected or breached duties.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Residential PEEPs enforcement notice
verified_claims: An enforcement notice under Article 30 of the Fire Safety Order may be served for non-compliance with duties under the Order or regulations made under it.
limitations: A notice requires authority-specific evidence and procedure and must not be inferred from missing public data.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Residential PEEPs dispute route
verified_claims: Fire and Rescue Authorities and the Residents Voice process are not expected to arbitrate individual disagreements; complaints, ombudsman or housing-authority routes may be appropriate.
limitations: The correct dispute route depends on tenure, issue and legal context.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Toolkit availability outside policy scope
verified_claims: The Responsible Persons toolkit is intended for all responsible persons, including those whose buildings fall outside the Residential PEEPs policy scope.
limitations: Toolkit availability does not extend the Regulations to an out-of-scope building.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Toolkit examples and deployment boundary
verified_claims: The toolkit collates real-life initiatives and case studies that responsible persons may consider for their own buildings.
limitations: Case studies are examples, not universal specifications or proof of suitability for another building.

sources.name: Responsible-person assessor selection and liability
verified_claims: The responsible person remains legally liable for a suitable and sufficient fire-risk assessment and should document due diligence when selecting a competent assessor.
limitations: Membership, insurance or references alone do not prove competence for a particular premises.
